title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: Why DHA matters for fetal development, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements.
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA
Omega-3 and DHA are two types of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) that are essential for the health of both mother and fetus. DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) is a particularly important type of omega-3 fatty acid for fetal brain and eye development.

## Role of DHA in Pregnancy
DHA plays a crucial role in the formation and development of the fetal brain and eyes. It also helps support the development of the fetal heart and immune system. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA is one of the most important nutrients for fetal development.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
There are many food sources rich in Omega-3 and DHA that pregnant women can include in their diet. Some of these food sources include:
- Salmon
- Tuna
- Sardines
- Anchovies
- Caviar
- Seaweed

## Precautions with Fish and Seafood
Pregnant women need to be cautious when consuming fish and seafood because some types may contain mercury, a toxic substance that can harm fetal development. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should limit their consumption of fish and seafood high in mercury, such as shark, swordfish, and king mackerel.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
Omega-3 and DHA supplements can be an option for pregnant women who are unable to get enough of these nutrients from their diet. However, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements. According to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), pregnant women should take Omega-3 and DHA supplements under the guidance of their healthcare provider and not exceed the recommended dose.

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are two types of polyunsaturated fatty acids that are essential for the health of both mother and fetus. Pregnant women can get Omega-3 and DHA from their diet and supplements, but need to be cautious when consuming fish and seafood high in mercury and consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements. For more information on [pregnancy meal planning](/blog/topics) and [prenatal nutrition](/blog/dinh-duong-ba-bau), pregnant women can visit our website.

## When to Consult a Healthcare Provider
Pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider if they have any questions or concerns about using Omega-3 and DHA during pregnancy. Their healthcare provider can provide personalized information and guidance on the safe and effective use of Omega-3 and DHA.
